# Derivation 3.7B — Directional and completion boundaries {#sec-derivation-03-07B-completion-boundaries .unnumbered}

## Purpose

This appendix records the inherited transverse-vector PDE as a provisional
field seed and localizes the remaining nonlinear, tensor, radiative, and
rotating-source burdens.

## Role, regime, and status

- **Role:** maturity and completion ledger.
- **Regime:** weak nonstationary response and downstream extensions.
- **Status:** vector PDE provisional; higher layers open.
- **Non-claim:** no physical vector mode, nonlinear coefficient family,
  tensor source, waveform, or exact rotating solution is promoted here.

## Provisional vector seed

The inherited transverse equation is

$$
\boxed{
\Box \mathcal A_i
=-\frac{16\pi G_N}{c^3}j_i^\perp,
\qquad
\partial_i\mathcal A_i=0}.
\tag{3.7B.1}
$$

As a PDE, Equation (3.7B.1) has the retarded Green form

$$
\mathcal A_i(t_*,\mathbf x)
=-\frac{4G_N}{c^3}\int
\frac{j_i^\perp(t_*-R/c,\mathbf x')}{R}\,d^3x'.
\tag{3.7B.2}
$$

Its stationary limit recovers the inherited transverse Poisson equation. In
the selected positive-action normalization only, this gives
$\mathcal A_i=-4\theta_i^\perp$. Here $\mathcal A_i$ labels the propagating
action/PDE coordinate. It is not the provisional observer-facing Chapter shift
$A_i$ of Derivation 3.5A, is not identified with a physical observer shift,
and is not a universal readout map. These facts establish field-side
consistency only.

The physical promotion gate remains failed. For a single positive reciprocal
vector action, the source sign, work ledger, mass-shell metric dictionary, and
rotating-source solution combine to reverse the physical Lense--Thirring
orientation. A tested elliptic constrained response can repair the stationary
sign only by fitting a coefficient and introduces no stage-causal observable
map. Promoting the compensator to a healthy causal propagating sector returns
the positive-bundle sign obstruction.

Equation (3.7B.1) therefore does not yet support:

- a physical ordinary-matter vector mode count;
- a closed source--carrier work exchange;
- a transported observer-axis law;
- a vector radiation observable; or
- a rotating-source prediction.

## Completion ledger

| Layer | Present object | What is established | What remains open |
|---|---|---|---|
| stationary scalar | $\Delta\theta_0=-(4\pi G_N/c^3)\mathcal M$ | Poisson/Newtonian map | interacting source allocation and physical $\gamma=1$ ruler |
| nonstationary scalar | Derivation 3.7A | positive point-carrier mode, retarded solution, reciprocal point-carrier work | bound matter, emission, screening, empirical viability |
| stationary directional | $\Delta\theta_i^\perp=-(4\pi G_N/c^3)j_i^\perp$ | field-side target and $|\kappa|=4$ endpoint | positive causal action/readout orientation |
| nonstationary directional | $\mathcal A_i$ in Equation (3.7B.1) | provisional PDE seed | physical source, work, axes, radiation |
| nonlinear scalar/spatial | no adopted equation | none beyond selected scalar clock package | field equations, constraints, moderate/strong regime |
| tensor sector | no adopted source/action | none | physical modes, source law, backreaction, waveforms |
| rotating source | weak endpoint only | Lense--Thirring regression target | native stationary solution; exact Kerr remains open |

## What is not carried forward

Earlier completion notes assigned unity defaults to nonlinear scalar and shift
self-sources and wrote a transverse-traceless wave slot with a familiar
normalization. Those expressions were provisional ansatz families. No reviewed
action, constraint count, source law, or observer map promoted them. They are
therefore omitted from the candidate trust layer rather than preserved as a
near-complete ladder.

## Reopening conditions

Directional promotion requires a complete construction that fixes its
coefficient before endpoint comparison and supplies:

1. positive physical modes or healthy constraints;
2. one reciprocal current and work ledger;
3. causal response for time-dependent sources;
4. explicit carrier and observer-axis transport; and
5. the required rotating-source orientation.

Tensor, nonlinear, and radiative work should open only after its source,
action, constraint, and observable objects are specified. Retarded solutions
or familiar coefficients alone are not enough.

## Result

The nonstationary scalar candidate is the only action-supported time-dependent
sector in the present appendix packet. The vector equation remains a PDE seed,
and nonlinear, tensor, radiative, and exact rotating completion remain open
research layers.
